<!-- https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/platform/faq/ -->

# FAQ
_Short answers, each pointing at the doc that proves it._
Last verified: 2026-08-27

- **Will this brick my gun?** No. Stock firmware is never touched, and everything is sent over the documented Bluetooth serial protocol. A power-cycle restores any tagger, and Battle Company's USB updater is the factory-restore path. The tools refuse malformed frames and ask for explicit confirmation for anything outside the known-safe command list. A `panic` command (`$CLEAR,*` then `$SP,99,*`) returns a gun to a sane state.
- **Do I need to solder?** Not for Tier 0 or Tier 1, which use a laptop and the phones you own. The Companion prototype builds with **zero soldering** on a breadboard kit. A wearable unit is about 7 easy through-hole joints, or none if you pick an ESP32-S3 board with onboard LiPo charging. There is also an off-the-shelf route (an M5StickC-class module + IR unit + battery, ~$30–35, no fabrication).
- **Does it work on iPhone?** Yes. The player app is native (Capacitor + CoreBluetooth), so iOS is first-class. What does *not* work is Web Bluetooth in any iOS browser, which is exactly why the app is native. Install is a one-time step: a free Apple ID gives 7-day on-device builds, then sideload or TestFlight for sharing. ✅ (the app ran on an iPhone X against real taggers on 2026-08-25)
- **How many guns can one laptop run?** In laptop-only Tier 0, two things are proven. One laptop radio held a 2-gun scored match, and a 3-gun synced start. The maximum number of BLE links per radio is untested. On any real field, give each gun its own phone. The laptop then holds zero gun links during play.
- **How many players and teams?** Up to **63** player slots per game (wire ids 1–63; the gun accepts 0–63 and Open BRX reserves 0) and **4** native hardware teams (with on-gun friendly-fire protection). More squads than four? Put everyone on one team, wear armbands, and let Mission Control score logical teams. There is no on-gun friendly-fire protection in that mode.
- **Do I need internet or venue Wi-Fi?** No. The field is an island: a laptop and a $20 battery travel router (or a laptop hotspot for small games) make the LAN. No SIM, no cloud, no internet. Nodes keep playing with the Wi-Fi dead and sync when they are back in range.
- **Why don't I see my kill instantly on a big field?** Because a kill is only visible from the victim's gun. It has to reach Mission Control and come back to the shooter's phone. You always know you died right away. Your kill confirm can wait until you are back in coverage. The Companion mesh (M6) is the fix for instant field-wide feedback. 🧪/
- **Does the gun still play its own kill sounds and green sight flash?** In a host-configured game the gun goes quiet by itself. But the flash (`$SFLASH`) and the announcer audio (`$PLAY`) are BLE-drivable, and our stack drives them exactly the way the official app does.
- **Can I still use the official Callsign app afterwards?** Yes, because nothing on the gun changes. One caution: opening Callsign resets a renamed gun's `$NAME` back to the default. Re-stamp it with `python -m brx_mcp rename`.
- **Which BRX generations work?** Gen 2/3 (BLE, Nordic UART) are the supported path. Gen 1 taggers use Bluetooth Classic serial, which the BLE-only library does not speak. A serial-port guide is still to do. ✅/
- **Do my Smart Grenades work with it?** Yes, for $0: five native objective modes set by the on-grenade button (Frag / Assault / Hill / Respawn / CTF). Hill and Respawn state is readable live over BLE. The mode itself cannot be set over BLE.
- **Can I add my own sounds?** Yes. The tagger's 2,166-id sound bank is decoded. Custom packs swap over the USB port (hold SELECT at boot → `AUDIO` folder). A Companion with a microSD would give unlimited custom audio. ✅/
- **Does the gun show my score?** The BRX has no screen. The phone HUD (or later a Companion HUD) is your score, ammo, lives and respawn timer. The gun's own sight flash and speaker give you the hit and kill feel.
- **Is this affiliated with Battle Company?** No. Open BRX is an independent open-source project, and "BRX" is used descriptively to name the hardware it serves. Protocol discovery credit goes to LaserTagMods.
- **What's the licence?** MIT, covering software, specs, and (as they land) firmware and STLs.
Source: README.md §Safety, mcp/brx_mcp/protocol.py · hardware/brx-companion-spec.md §Sourcing · docs/adr/0003-native-app-over-web-bluetooth.md, docs/handoff-ios-ble-findings.md, app/README.md, docs/mode-limits.md §Platform · docs/architecture-topology.md §2 + §7, docs/FOLLOWUPS.md B10 · docs/game-modes.md §Team structure · docs/adr/0002-laptop-mission-control-host.md · docs/architecture-topology.md §5 · protocol/brx-protocol.md §7o, docs/experiment-log.md 2026-08-26 "$SFLASH validated from OUR stack" · docs/HANDOFF.md §Fleet ops rules · README.md §Platform notes · docs/reference/grenade.md, docs/game-modes.md §Grenade · protocol/callsign-extract/sound-bank.md, docs/build-tiers.md Tier 0 · docs/VISION.md §How much can we get out of the BRX · docs/VISION.md §Naming, README.md §Credit · LICENSE

<!-- https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/ -->

# Meet the BRX
name every part of the tagger, headset and accessories. Explain what each light and port means. Show why the BRX is a simple IR instrument that remembers nothing, which every later section builds on.

- [The BRX at a glance](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/overview/): A laser tagger shaped like a rifle, a wireless sensor headset, and a smart grenade. Plus what they are not.
- [The tagger, part by part](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/tagger/): Every button, port, emitter and light on the rifle, and what each one is really for.
- [The IR emitter, the sight, and the sensors](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/ir-and-sensors/): The invisible beam that carries every tag. Here are the published specs and what we measured.
- [Lights and what they mean](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/leds/): The gun's LED bank and the headset's ring. Read them like a dashboard.
- [The headset](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/headset/): A wireless sensor band that decides whether your tagger is allowed to shoot.
- [Battery and power](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/battery/): A 7.4 V two-cell pack with one nasty surprise: the connector polarity is backwards.
- [Generations: which BRX do you have?](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/generations/): Gen1 speaks Bluetooth Classic; Gen2 and Gen3 speak BLE. Here is how to tell in 30 seconds.
- [Grenade and accessories](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/accessories/): What each add-on physically is. How to use them lives in the Accessories & Stations section.
- [Spec sheet and what's in the box](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/hardware/spec-sheet/): One page to print. It lists the exact parts, numbers and kit contents for the tagger, the headset and the grenade.

# Operating the BRX
get you from "box on the table" to "a game running and understood". Every button hold, every LED and every voice line should mean something to you. Anything that needs a laptop, a cable, or the BLE protocol is pointed at the developer section, not explained here.

- [Quick Start](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/quick-start/): From the box to your first "TARGET MODE" voice line in about fifteen minutes, plus a charge.
- [Charging & Batteries](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/power/): Two ports on the gun, two kinds of charger, one polarity trap.
- [The On-Gun Menu](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/on-gun-menu/): Everything you can set without a phone, and what the gun remembers.
- [Indoor vs Outdoor Mode](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/indoor-outdoor/): One three-second hold changes your range, your LEDs and your blast radius.
- [Sighting the Laser](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/sighting/): Target mode makes the gun harmless, tireless, and honest about where it points.
- [Pairing the Headset](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/headset-pairing/): The number one cause of "my gun won't fire", and the fix for it.
- [The Grenade & Other Accessories](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/accessories/): Pair a thrown grenade, or use it as a respawn point, a hill or a flag. No app needed.
- [The Callsign App](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/callsign-app/): Battle Company's official phone app: what it does, how you build a game, and the three things nobody tells you.
- [Running a Native Game on Stock Kit](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/stock-game/): A walkthrough of a whole match, on-gun or app-hosted, and what every light and voice line means while it runs.
- [Range & Line of Sight](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/range/): What the numbers on the box mean once the sun comes out.
- [Care & Storage](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/operate/care/): Keep it charged, keep it dry, and turn it off between rounds.

# Gameplay
be the one place that lists the whole Callsign arsenal with real numbers. It explains the damage model in player words. It lists every stock mode and setting, so nobody has to scroll a carousel or dig through PDFs again.

- [What the BRX can play](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/overview/): Two arsenals, three ways to run a game, and one damage model underneath all of it
- [The complete Callsign arsenal](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/weapons/): Every weapon the official app can hand you (19 weapons, 20 captured frames), with the numbers it actually sends
- [Health, armor & damage](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/health/): What a hit takes away, what armor does, and why nothing comes back on its own
- [How a kill actually works](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/how-a-kill-works/): From trigger pull to green flash in five steps (the developer section has the bit layout)
- [Native game modes & their settings](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/modes/): Everything the gun's own menu and the Callsign app will run, with the exact option values
- [Classes, factions, perks & killstreaks](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/classes-and-perks/): What Supremacy's characters are made of, what the ALT button cycles, and what the app hands out for streaks
- [The Smart Grenade's game modes](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/grenade-modes/): Five objective modes, one button, one colour, and which ones the guns can actually "see"
- [Beyond stock: the Open BRX mode catalog](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/gameplay/open-brx-modes/): The gun keeps no game state, so any rule you can write over hits, teams, health and spawns is a mode. This is a taste; the full catalog lives in the platform section.

# Sound, voice & updates
show how BRX audio works from end to end (who plays what, how loud, and how to change it), publish the first complete searchable map of the 2166-id sound bank, and walk through the USB sound-pack and firmware update path, with Battle Company's updater as the factory restore.

- [How BRX audio works](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/sound/how-it-works/): One speaker, two triggers: what the gun plays by itself, and what a host tells it to play
- [Voice packs & announcers](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/sound/voice-packs/): Male, Female, Heavy, Medic, Valkyrie. Every character is a set of sound-bank slots
- [The sound bank](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/sound/sound-bank/): All 2166 ids the BRX will play, by family, with durations and the meanings the community has pinned
- [Custom sounds over USB](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/sound/custom-sounds/): Yes, you can put your own audio on a BRX. No firmware hacking, and fully reversible
- [Firmware updates & factory restore](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/sound/firmware/): The same USB disk carries the firmware. Here is the official procedure, and the traps
- [Volume](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/sound/volume/): On-gun 1–5, protocol 0–100, and why "30" is silence

# Fix, mod & accessorise
get a broken tagger back into a game in under five minutes with symptom-first ladders; write down the repairs and mods the community really does (with credit); list the accessories and the places owners gather; answer the ten questions every owner asks.

- [Diagnose my tagger](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/diagnose/): Start with what you see. Pick the ladder that matches, then work down it. The headset is the first thing to check.
- [Headset, pairing & Bluetooth](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/pairing/): The headset controls everything: firing, joining a game, and whether a phone can hold a connection.
- [Hits, sound & battery](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/hits-sound-battery/): When the gun fires but nothing lands, nothing is heard, or nothing lasts.
- [Repairs](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/repairs/): What owners fix themselves, what Battle Company sells, and what's a send-it-back.
- [Mods](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/mods/): The community norm is "no permanent modification". Everything rides on the phone bracket or clips to the rail.
- [Accessories](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/accessories/): Grenade, stations, headsets, power and mounts. What each one is, and the gotchas nobody tells you.
- [The community](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/community/): Where BRX owners really solve things, and what each place is good for.
- [FAQ](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/fix/faq/): The questions owners ask first.

<!-- https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/ -->

# Developer reference
the complete interoperability spec for the BRX tagger + headset: transport, framing, every known command and event with its field map, the `$WEAP` / `$GSET` / `$PSET` / `$SIR` tables, the optical IR word, the USB console, and a copy-paste path from `pip install` to a live game. Every row says how sure we are of the fact it carries.

- [Transport, framing & safety](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/transport/): How you reach the gun, what a frame looks like, and why nothing here can brick one. Start here if you want your own code to talk to a tagger.
- [Command reference](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/commands/): Every command we know of, with args, meaning and confidence: host → tagger, tagger → host, and headset. This page lists every frame you can send the gun. Copy them exactly as written.
- [The arm sequence: from `$CLEAR` to a live gun](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/arm-sequence/): The exact frame order that takes a tagger live, respawns it, and ends the game. Send these frames in this order. We captured the order from the official app and reproduced it with our own host.
- [`$WEAP`: the weapon definition](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/weap/): Forty-odd comma-separated tokens that make a weapon out of data: damage, cadence, fire mode, ammo, sounds, IR type. This page maps every token, so you can build a weapon of your own.
- [`$GSET` and `$PSET`: game and player settings](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/gset-pset/): The two frames that set on-gun rules and the player's pools, identity and voice pack. Read this page to give each player their health, armor and id.
- [`$SIR`: the incoming-IR effects matrix](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/sir/): What an IR hit does to this gun is decided by the victim's table, not by the shooter's weapon. This page shows how to write that table.
- [Events: what the gun tells you](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/events/): Hits, health, HUD echoes, buttons and telemetry, plus the proof that the gun keeps no game state. Read this page to learn what the gun sends back to your code.
- [The IR word: what a shot carries through the air](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/ir/): A 25-bit pulse-width-encoded word on a 38 kHz carrier, decoded from LaserTagMods' base-station source and verified on our own receiver and emitter. Read this page if you are building your own IR sender or receiver.
- [The USB serial console: `QUERY` and `SETUP`](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/serial-console/): The micro-USB "Programing Port" is a Teensy serial console with two commands, not the `$` protocol and not SSH. Plug a tagger into a computer and this page tells you what you can ask it.
- [Headset, link and what survives](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/headset-link/): Which state lives where, and what a BLE drop, a headset switch-off, or a power-cycle each wipe. Read this page before you write code that reconnects to a gun.
- [Getting started with `brx-mcp`](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/brx-mcp/): From `pip install` to a live game in six commands, plus the MCP tools for driving a gun from an AI agent. Start here to get a working setup fast.
- [Captures: recording and decoding the official app](https://open-brx.iamrossi.workers.dev/manual/dev/captures/): How every fact on these pages was obtained, and how to take the next one. Read this page if you want to record the app yourself.
